checks: The positive total gives m>0. Each tail contains at least one value ≥m, since otherwise the measurable positive deficit integrates positively. These two points belong to the convex positive set, and their transformed values are at least the transform of m.

Root and logarithm are increasing. Concavity therefore gives f≥m throughout the middle interval. Its exact average is m, and continuity on the interior of the concavity domain gives a plateau on the open middle interval.

A transformed value larger than the plateau outside it would force an intermediate plateau point above the plateau by strict convex weighting. Thus f≤m on the positive set and also on its zero complement, so each tail equality gives f=m almost everywhere. Endpoints of the domain and values on null sets cause no extra assumption.
readability: The proof and its scope are clear.

summary: The matched positive tail means force a plateau in the middle, and concavity forces equality on both tails almost everywhere.
